question: Which evidence supports using context routing rather than vector recall or long-context prompting alone?

candidate_papers.title: Vector Recall Is Not Context Routing
candidate_papers.text: Vector retrieval can find similar papers, but it does not guarantee that only selected evidence reaches the reader or that verifier feedback triggers recovery.

candidate_papers.title: PaperServe: Context Frontiers for Evidence-Bounded Readers
candidate_papers.text: Context routing forms an explicit evidence frontier. The reader sees selected papers only, while the verifier can demand retrieval recovery if the gold paper is missing.

candidate_papers.title: Long Context Windows Without Evidence Selection
candidate_papers.text: A long-context reader may accept many retrieved papers at once, increasing attention dilution when irrelevant papers are included.

candidate_papers.title: Training a Policy for Paper Search
candidate_papers.text: A reinforcement learner may optimize paper selection over time, but this fixture expects deterministic dependency-free routing.

expected_answer_points: Context routing is not equivalent to vector recall.
Context routing is not equivalent to merely expanding the reader context window.
The selected evidence frontier and verifier recovery are the differentiators.
